title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector response to Conflict Affected Communities in the Oromia region, Kelem Wellega zones, Dembi Dollo Town.

description.narrative: ltpgtTo support the IDP and host communities in the Oromia region, Kelem Wellega zone, Dembi Dollo Town, Action Against Hunger, partnering with the Action for Social Development and Environmental Protection Organization (ASDEPO) (local implementing partner), designed a multi-sector humanitarian response that encompasses cash for rent(CFR), agriculture, nutrition, health, WASH, and protection as mainstream. It is believed that the provision of this multi-sectoral response will support the overall effort provided in the selected areas of the sectors for the beneficiaries. The action will support a total of 62,217 beneficiaries (women: 18,006, men: 14,172, girls: 15,465, boys: 14,574). Through the distribution of cash for rent(CFR) a total of 11,148 beneficiaries will be addressed . Similarly, this initiative will support 3,898 IDPs and 9,094 host communities from Dembi Dolo Town through Supporting early identification and referral of acute malnutrition through mass MUAC screening integrated with Vitamin A supplementation, de-worming, and GBV referral services supporting health health facilities on the treatment of severe acute malnutrition with complications in SC strengthening referral linkage services in accordance with the national protocol and SPHERE standard supporting health facilities in the treatment of severe acute malnutrition without complications in OTP supporting the implementation of a family MUAC approach and promotion and supporting the protection and support of maternity and similar nutrition support initiatives. Through the health sector, the action will reach 13,977 (4,193 IDPs and 9,784 host communities) at Dembi Tolo Town through supporting health facilities to provide primary health care services, revitalization of services in damaged health posts, organizing outreach programs for IDPs, supporting catch immunization campaigns, integrating MISP services, supporting GBV referral services and linkages with local government services (particularly BoWSA and Health), risk communication and community engagement activities, building the capacity of health services, providing clinical management of GBV, public health emergency management and disease surveillance, and other key guidelines such as IMNCI. The initiative will also support 2100 IDPs through cash intervention and 2,500 individuals through agricultural commodity distribution in Dembi Tolo Town. The WASH activities are in line with the prioritized activities per the allocation strategy and in line with addressing the needs of IDPs and host communities in Dembi Dolo town. The proposed WASH initiatives include rehabilitation and expansion of nonfunctional water schemes, capacity building for Water Management Committees (WASHCOs) and water offices and utilities, Construction of basic sanitation facilities (sex-segregated VIP latrines, hand washing stations) in protracted IDP sites, distribution of life-saving WASH NFIs and water treatment supplies, and hygiene and sanitation promotion initiatives ltbrgtlt/pgt
